name: Roast pork tenderloin with sweet potatoes and date-feta relish
intro: A whole tenderloin roasted beside sweet potatoes, sliced while it's still blushing pink, and covered in a salty, sweet relish of dates, feta, lemon, and chile.

steps.text: Heat the oven. Toss the sweet potatoes and pepper with oil and salt and spread them on a sheet pan.
Roast the vegetables on their own first.
Rub the pork with oil and salt. For a browned outside, sear it first in a hot oiled skillet, 2 minutes a side. Lay it in the middle of the pan and roast until the thickest part reads 140°F.
Meanwhile, make the relish: the dates, the feta, the zest and juice of the lemon, a pinch of chile flakes, and 3 tbsp olive oil, stirred together.
Take the pork out at 140°F and let it rest 10 minutes; it finishes at about 145°F, still just pink in the middle.
Slice it thick over the sweet potatoes and arugula, and spoon the relish over everything.

how_it_works: Lean meat has almost no fat to keep it juicy or carry flavor, so the richness goes on at the end instead: a relish of olive oil, salty feta, and sweet dates does what a fattier cut would do on its own. The other half of the lesson is pulling it early — pork is at its best slightly pink.
swaps: Thick pork chops, seared hard, take the same relish.
No feta? Salt the relish a little more.
Extra relish is good on roasted squash or spread on toast.
leftovers: Sliced pork and sweet potatoes over 1 cup of cooked rice, with the leftover relish, is two lunches.

sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart — USDA
sources.note: whole pork cuts are safe at 145°F with a 3-minute rest

nutrition.serving: A third of the recipe: about 6 oz pork, sweet potatoes and peppers, relish, arugula.
nutrition.excludes: Rice. The lunches go over 1 cup cooked rice: add about 200 kcal and 45 g carbohydrate.
